intro: Welcome back to the kitchen, viewers! Every day the dice roll a premise and a dozen constraints, and the game has to use all of them. Today's roll was seed 2285291030. Here's each ingredient, and what we cooked with it.

rolls.became: Wibble, a flying saucer who hosts Wibble's Little Kitchen, the top cooking show on a planet where everyone is the size of a peppercorn. Jittery is live-TV nerves: the saucer wobbles, the beam shakes, and the whole week started because Wibble's nerves knocked a dial.

On a planet of peppercorn-sized viewers, the show's whole gimmick is taking a big Earth dish and shrinking it to plate size with the saucer's ray. That's also why the crew is paid in bites: one regulation bite feeds a stagehand for a week.

Noodle week. Live on air, Wibble knocked the shrink ray to GROW on the pot and the dial snapped off. Now the giant pot keeps boiling over, pushing giant noodles out across a borrowed Earth kitchen's counter, toward the sink.

You steer the saucer: move the mouse over the kitchen, drag, or use the arrow keys. Whatever noodle is under the beam shrinks. Later the Autopilot flies itself to the fattest noodle whenever you let go.

Every boil-over is a wave of noodles slithering for the sink. Sous-saucers, little drones from the planet's top culinary school, hover over the counter and zap whatever passes under them on their own. If one noodle lands in the sink, that boil-over goes again from the top.

rolls.value: reset loop (prestige for a permanent bonus)
rolls.became: Each day is one episode. Once you reach the day's running order, you can wrap the episode: the counter is mopped and the props go back, but the episode airs back home overnight and the fans write in. Fan Mail buys things that stay all week: a Fan Club, a Tip Jar, a Standing Crew.

Noodles left out on the counter keep drinking and go soggy: they swell, up to three times their length, and get fat and dotty. A soggy noodle pays no more than a firm one, so you steer to the fat ones first. A Cold Rinse, a Colander and an Ice Bath slow it down. And the thing that broke is the ray's dial, which is why the pot never stops.
A letter on the wall: Inspector E. of the G.B.R. will visit on Sunday to certify your noodles. The calendar on the wall is the meter: seven episodes, Monday to Sunday, one wrap a day.
Inspector Eunice. Wibble read G.B.R. as some sort of health board and decided every noodle had to be back to regulation size before she arrived.
Eunice, the inspector: tall, kind, very precise, carrying a tape measure.
Noodle lengths in centimetres. They start at 20 cm, and by Sunday each boil-over is pushing out kilometres of noodle and the bites in the bowl run into the millions.
A whole week of episodes, about four to six hours of play. While you're off air the sous-saucers keep zapping at a fraction of the rate (for up to six hours), and they tell you what you missed.

Everything is one ink on one paper: windows with striped title bars and close boxes, MacPaint dither patterns for every grey, a clapperboard button with the thick default ring. Pixelify Sans and Silkscreen for the type. The turkey and the trophy are icons pixelated down to two colours.
Eight parchment browns by JustJimmy. The darkest is the ink and the lightest is the paper; two tans make the checkered desktop behind the windows.

A slow dub groove, deep sub bass and offbeat chords with echo, all in the whole-tone scale, the classic floaty spaceship sound. It fills out as the week goes on and gets tense on Sunday. Every zap, plink and doorbell is on the same scale.
Wibble narrates like a cooking-show host: "Here's one I shrank earlier", "Gently, gently... and done", "Don't worry if yours went a bit soggy: nobody at home can tell."

rolls.value: a household ritual of that time of year
rolls.became: The game came out the day before Thanksgiving. The family whose kitchen Wibble borrowed has left their turkey thawing in the sink in cold water. The packet says change the water every 30 minutes, so you can pay to do exactly that. It does nothing. Wibble takes it very seriously.

rolls.value: it was the wrong goal all along
rolls.became: G.B.R. is the Galactic Book of Records. The viewers had written in about the biggest noodles they'd ever seen ("THE BIG ONES ARE THE BEST", says the fan drawing), and Eunice came to certify the longest noodle ever grown. Wibble spent the whole week shrinking a world record. The clues were up all along: the crest on the letter is a little trophy, the ruler, and a fan who'd told "the Records people".

On Sunday the pot heaves out the Big One, far too big to shrink. You try anyway, and then the doorbell goes, on the dot. The ray is switched off at the wall, the saucer drifts down on its own, and the ending plays itself: Eunice certifies whatever you hadn't got round to shrinking.

outro: And that's all we've got time for. Do try this at home, but please turn the pot off.
